title: A knowledge-guided agentic framework for mitigating patient-context ambiguity in health queries
summary: Patients often submit short, underspecified queries to healthcare chatbots that lack the patient-specific information needed to determine an appropriate response. Although these queries may be linguistically clear, they can support multiple plausible answers depending on undisclosed factors such as symptoms, diagnoses, medications, allergies, or dietary restrictions. A language model answering such a query directly may therefore rely on unsupported assumptions about the patient. We introduce a knowledge-guided agentic framework for mitigating patient-context ambiguity before final response generation. The framework operates between the patient and an otherwise unchanged downstream language model. It interprets the initial query, uses a task-specific knowledge graph to construct a set of plausible hypotheses, identifies the missing patient-context variables needed to distinguish among them, and asks targeted follow-up questions. The original query and the acquired context are then combined into a clarified prompt for the downstream model. We evaluated the framework across five language models using two controlled ambiguity-mitigation benchmarks: diagnosis retrieval from 1,034 symptom queries with clinically relevant evidence systematically masked, and dietary-safety classification from 487 queries with decisive health context omitted. The framework was compared with direct answering of the underspecified query and with rephrasing the same query without acquiring new patient information. In diagnosis retrieval, it increased overall exact Top-1 accuracy by at least 57.1 percentage points and selective exact Recall@5 by at least 77.7 percentage points across the five evaluated models compared with direct prompting. In dietary-safety classification, it improved accuracy across all five models and achieved the highest Matthews correlation coefficient for four...
tldr: The paper introduces a knowledge-guided agentic framework that identifies missing patient context in underspecified health queries by generating plausible hypotheses, asking targeted follow-up questions, and combining the acquired context with the original query before passing it to a downstream language model, significantly improving diagnosis retrieval and dietary-safety classification accuracy.
tldr_zh: 该论文提出了一种知识引导的智能体框架，通过生成合理假设、提出针对性追问来识别未指定的患者上下文，并将获取的上下文与原始查询合并后再传递给下游语言模型，在诊断检索和饮食安全分类上显著提升了准确率。
summary_zh:
摘要：
患者向医疗健康聊天机器人提交的查询通常简短且信息不充分，缺乏确定适当回应所需的患者特定信息。尽管这些查询在语言上可能清晰，但由于未披露的症状、诊断、用药、过敏史或饮食限制等因素，它们可能支持多个合理的答案。直接回答此类查询的语言模型因此可能依赖于对患者未经证实的假设。我们提出了一种知识引导的智能体框架，旨在最终回应生成之前减轻患者上下文的模糊性。该框架在患者与一个未作其他改变的下游语言模型之间运行。它解释初始查询，使用特定任务的知识图谱构建一组合理的假设，识别区分这些假设所需的缺失患者上下文变量，并提出有针对性的追问问题。然后将原始查询与所获取的上下文合并，形成针对下游模型的澄清提示。我们使用两个受控的模糊性缓解基准，在五个语言模型上评估了该框架：从1034个症状查询中检索诊断（其中临床相关证据被系统性地遮蔽），以及从487个省略了关键健康背景的查询中进行饮食安全分类。将框架与直接回答不充分查询以及在不获取新患者信息的情况下改写同一查询进行了比较。在诊断检索中，与直接提示相比，该框架在五个评估模型上使整体精确Top-1准确率至少提高了57.1个百分点，选择性精确召回率@5至少提高了77.7个百分点。在饮食安全分类中，该框架在所有五个模型上均提升了准确率，并在四个模型上取得了最高的马修斯相关系数……

title: Towards Surgical World-Action Modeling: A Preliminary Joint Visual-Trajectory Forecasting for Surgical Motion Planning
summary: Reliable surgical planning requires models to anticipate not only how instruments will move, but also how the operative visual state will evolve together with such motion. Existing approaches typically treat future scene generation and instrument trajectory prediction as two separate tasks. Scene-only models cannot directly evaluate the accuracy of future instrument motion at the trajectory level, while trajectory-only models fail to capture the visual consequences of instrument movement, leaving the consistency between predicted trajectories and future scene evolution unaddressed. Jointly forecasting both provides a more complete account of surgical action-scene dynamics by enabling explicit trajectory-level evaluation while simultaneously modeling the corresponding visual evolution. To bridge this gap, we present a preliminary joint visual-trajectory world-action model that simultaneously forecasts future visual states and instrument trajectories from historical surgical observations. Specifically, we encode historical video frames and tool trajectories into latent representations, which are processed by a temporal-spatial encoder and subsequently decoded through separate visual-state and trajectory prediction heads. Based on this preliminary architecture, a chunked autoregressive rollout is repeatedly applied to predict fifteen future steps. The chunked strategy consistently outperforms direct one-shot prediction across all evaluated horizons, improving first-segment PSNR from 18.86 to 23.11 dB and reducing ADE from 45.77 to 22.22 pixels. These results demonstrate the initial feasibility of joint visual-motion forecasting. However, we observe progressive visual degradation and accumulated trajectory errors over longer prediction horizons, which remain important challenges for future surgical world-action modeling.
tldr: This paper proposes a joint visual-trajectory forecasting model for surgical motion planning, which simultaneously predicts future visual states and instrument trajectories from historical observations using a chunked autoregressive rollout, showing initial feasibility but with challenges in long-horizon prediction.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种用于手术运动规划的联合视觉-轨迹预测模型，能够同时从历史观测中预测未来的视觉状态和器械轨迹，采用分块自回归滚动生成方法，初步验证了可行性，但在长时域预测中仍存在视觉退化和轨迹累积误差问题。
summary_zh: 可靠的术前规划要求模型不仅能预测器械的运动轨迹，还需预见手术视觉状态随该运动的演变过程。现有方法通常将未来场景生成与器械轨迹预测视为两个独立任务。仅场景模型无法在轨迹层级直接评估未来器械运动的准确性，而仅轨迹模型则难以捕捉器械运动带来的视觉变化，导致预测轨迹与未来场景演变之间的一致性无法得到保障。联合预测两者可通过在显式评估轨迹精度的同时建模对应的视觉演变，从而更完整地刻画手术动作-场景动态。为弥补这一不足，我们提出一种初步的联合视觉-轨迹世界动作模型，该模型能从历史手术观测中同时预测未来视觉状态与器械轨迹。具体而言，我们将历史视频帧与工具轨迹编码为潜在表征，经由时空编码器处理后，分别通过独立的视觉状态预测头与轨迹预测头进行解码。基于这一初步架构，我们反复应用分块自回归展开以预测未来15个时间步。在所有评估时段上，分块策略始终优于直接一步预测，将第一分段的峰值信噪比从18.86 dB提升至23.11 dB，并将平均位移误差从45.77像素降至22.22像素。这些结果验证了联合视觉-运动预测的初步可行性。然而，我们观察到随着预测时段延长，视觉质量逐渐退化且轨迹误差不断累积，这对未来的手术世界动作建模仍是重要挑战。

title: Prompt-Conditioned Channel Attention for Hierarchical Feature Modulation toward Anatomy-Agnostic Segmentation
summary: Anatomically plausible segmentation remains challenging because of low contrast, ambiguous boundaries, and modality-specific artifacts. Interactive segmentation has emerged as a promising strategy to guide feature extraction and improve localization, particularly in structurally ambiguous regions. However, existing methods integrate prompts through late-stage fusion and lack explicit mechanisms for prompt-driven channel-wise modulation across hierarchical feature representations, limiting their ability to capture deeper contextual and modality-specific variations. To address these limitations, we introduce Prompt-Conditioned Channel Attention (PCCA), a novel modulation mechanism that enables deep, hierarchical integration of semantic prompts within encoder-decoder networks. PCCA extracts compact channel descriptors via pooling, projects them into a shared space, and fuses them through a gated excitation mechanism to compute prompt-aware channel attention weights. These weights adaptively recalibrate feature responses across multiple network stages, enabling prompt-conditioned, semantically enriched hierarchical representations. Building on this, we propose PROMISE-Net, instantiated in two network variants: a convolutional model (PROMISE-CNN) and a transformer-based model (PROMISE-Txformer). Across the ISIC-Lesion, Kvasir-Polyp, CAMUS-Cardiac, and Kvasir-Instrument benchmarks, integrating PCCA into PROMISE-CNN yielded relative IoU gains of 10.4%, 8.7%, 0.8%, and 3.4%, respectively, over the baseline U-Net, while PROMISE-Txformer achieved corresponding gains of 7.6%, 23.0%, 2.1%, and 1.1%, respectively, over the baseline UNETR. These results show consistent improvements across architectures, imaging modalities, and anatomical targets, establishing PCCA and PROMISE-Net as a scalable, generalizable framework for prompt-aware hierarchical feature modulation in medical image segmentation.
tldr: This paper introduces Prompt-Conditioned Channel Attention (PCCA), a novel mechanism for hierarchically integrating semantic prompts into encoder-decoder networks for medical image segmentation, achieving consistent improvements across multiple datasets and architectures.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种名为提示条件通道注意力（PCCA）的新机制，用于在编码器-解码器网络中分层整合语义提示，在多个医学图像分割数据集和架构上取得了一致的改进。
summary_zh:
摘要：  
由于低对比度、边界模糊以及模态特异性伪影，解剖学上合理的分割仍然具有挑战性。交互式分割已成为一种有前景的策略，用于引导特征提取并改善定位，尤其在结构模糊的区域中。然而，现有方法通过后期融合整合提示信息，缺乏在层次化特征表示中实现提示驱动的通道级调制的显式机制，限制了其捕获深层上下文及模态特异性变化的能力。为解决这些局限，我们提出提示条件通道注意力（PCCA）——一种新颖的调制机制，能够在编码器-解码器网络中实现语义提示的深度层次化整合。PCCA通过池化提取紧凑的通道描述符，将其投影到共享空间，并通过门控激励机制融合，以计算提示感知的通道注意力权重。这些权重自适应地重新校准多个网络阶段的特征响应，从而实现提示条件化的、语义丰富的层次化表示。在此基础上，我们提出PROMISE-Net，并实例化为两种网络变体：卷积模型（PROMISE-CNN）和基于Transformer的模型（PROMISE-Txformer）。在ISIC-Lesion、Kvasir-Polyp、CAMUS-Cardiac和Kvasir-Instrument基准测试中，将PCCA集成至PROMISE-CNN相比基线U-Net分别获得了10.4%、8.7%、0.8%和3.4%的相对IoU提升，而PROMISE-Txformer相比基线UNETR分别获得了7.6%、23.0%、2.1%和1.1%的相应提升。这些结果展示了在不同架构、成像模态和解剖目标上的一致改进，确立了PCCA和PROMISE-Net作为医学图像分割中提示感知层次化特征调制的可扩展、可泛化框架。

title: Artificial Intelligence for Workflow Analysis in Colorectal Surgery: A Multicentric, Cross-Procedural Development and Generalization Study
summary: Minimally invasive colorectal surgeries (MIS-CRS) are characterised by significant variability and inconsistent outcomes. ColoWorkflow, a tool for the video-based assessment (VBA) of MIS-CRS workflow, was recently validated. However, manual VBA is time-consuming, limiting implementation. This study presents AI-ColoWorkflow, a deep learning model for automated surgical workflow analysis across MIS-CRS. Operative videos of MIS-CRS were collected from 4 centres and a publicly available dataset. Phases and steps were manually annotated according to ColoWorkflow. A deep learning model combining a fine-tuned DINOv3 vision transformer for per-frame visual feature extraction with a hierarchical multi-stage temporal convolutional network was jointly optimized for phase and step recognition. The model trained on pooled multicentric data, namely AI-ColoWorkflow was compared against centre-specific and procedure-specific models on a held-out test set. The following metrics were used for evaluation: macro F1 score, balanced accuracy, precision, and recall. AI-ColoWorkflow achieved a macro F1 of 73.01% $\pm$ 10.27 (balanced accuracy 73.43%) for phase recognition and 39.82% $\pm$ 7.06 (balanced accuracy 38.65%) for step recognition. The global model outperformed centre- and procedure-specific models in most experiments except procedure-specific step recognition. In the generalization analysis, mean F1 was 48.42% for phase recognition. AI-ColoWorkflow can reliably recognize MIS-CRS phases. A single model trained on pooled, multicentric, multi-procedural data generalises at least as well as and often better than centre- or procedure-specific models for phase recognition in MIS-CRS, while procedure-specific step models retain advantages for certain procedure types, motivating hybrid training strategies for future surgical AI development.
tldr: This paper presents AI-ColoWorkflow, a deep learning model combining a DINOv3 vision transformer and hierarchical temporal convolutional network for automated phase and step recognition in minimally invasive colorectal surgery videos, demonstrating that a single multicentric model generalizes across centers and procedures.
tldr_zh: 本文提出AI-ColoWorkflow，一种结合DINOv3视觉变换器和分层多阶段时间卷积网络的深度学习模型，用于自动化识别微创结直肠手术视频中的手术阶段和步骤，证明了单一多中心模型能跨中心和手术方案泛化。
summary_zh: 微创结直肠手术（MIS-CRS）具有显著的变异性和不一致的临床结局。ColoWorkflow作为一种基于视频评估MIS-CRS工作流程的工具，近期已得到验证，但人工视频评估耗时较长，限制了其推广应用。本研究提出AI-ColoWorkflow——一种用于MIS-CRS全流程自动化手术工作流分析的深度学习模型。研究从4个中心和一个公开数据集收集MIS-CRS手术视频，根据ColoWorkflow对手术阶段和步骤进行人工标注。该深度学习模型结合了用于逐帧视觉特征提取的微调DINOv3视觉变换器与用于阶段及步骤识别的分层多阶段时序卷积网络，并进行了联合优化。在保留测试集上，基于多中心合并数据训练的全局模型（即AI-ColoWorkflow）与各中心特异性模型及各术式特异性模型进行了比较。采用以下指标进行评估：宏F1分数、平衡准确率、精确率和召回率。AI-ColoWorkflow在阶段识别上实现了宏F1为73.01%±10.27（平衡准确率73.43%），在步骤识别上为39.82%±7.06（平衡准确率38.65%）。除术式特异性步骤识别外，全局模型在大多数实验中均优于中心特异性和术式特异性模型。泛化分析中，阶段识别的平均F1为48.42%。AI-ColoWorkflow能够可靠识别MIS-CRS的手术阶段。基于多中心、多术式合并数据训练的单一模型在MIS-CRS阶段识别中的泛化能力至少与中心或术式特异性模型相当，且通常更优；而术式特异性步骤模型在特定术式类型中仍保持优势，这为未来手术人工智能的混合训练策略提供了依据。

title: RIPE++: Reinforced Keypoint Learning from Positive Pairs Only
summary: Sparse keypoint extraction and matching underpin core tasks in geometric computer vision, including structure-from-motion, visual SLAM, augmented reality, and medical image registration. Learning robust local feature representations, however, typically requires accurate camera poses or depth supervision, which are often unavailable in real-world settings. Reinforcement learning (RL) has recently emerged as a promising alternative, requiring only the information if two images show the same scene or not. However, existing RL formulations such as RIPE rely on coarse binary rewards and carefully constructed negative training pairs, limiting training stability and descriptor discriminability. In this paper, we revisit RL-based keypoint learning and propose a reward that fully exploits the geometric consistency signal, deriving both reward and penalty from a single positive pair without contrasting against negatives. This richer signal provides sufficient supervisory contrast to learn discriminative detectors and descriptors from positive image pairs alone, enabling representation learning under extremely limited supervision. Furthermore, we show that the same RL objective can be extended to the matching stage by adapting LightGlue, raising AUC@5 on MegaDepth1500 from 56.58 to 59.65 and enabling weakly-supervised training of the full sparse matching pipeline from image pairs with partial visual overlap. We validate our approach on established benchmarks, demonstrating competitive results compared to fully-supervised methods. We further show that the method can be even trained on low texture medical video sequences, where camera poses are usually unavailable and standard SfM pipelines often fail. Code and data are available at https://github.com/fraunhoferhhi/RIPEpp .
tldr: This paper proposes RIPE++, a reinforcement learning-based method for learning keypoints and descriptors from only positive image pairs, eliminating the need for negative pairs and achieving competitive results in geometric computer vision tasks including medical image registration.
tldr_zh: 本文提出RIPE++，一种基于强化学习的方法，仅使用正图像对学习关键点和描述符，无需负样本对，在包括医学图像配准在内的几何计算机视觉任务中取得了有竞争力的结果。
summary_zh:
摘要：  
稀疏关键点提取与匹配构成了几何计算机视觉中核心任务的基础，包括运动恢复结构、视觉SLAM、增强现实和医学图像配准。然而，学习鲁棒的局部特征表示通常需要准确的相机位姿或深度监督，这在现实场景中往往无法获取。强化学习（RL）最近作为一种有前景的替代方案出现，仅需知道两张图像是否显示同一场景的信息。然而，现有的RL公式（如RIPE）依赖于粗糙的二元奖励和精心构建的负训练对，限制了训练稳定性和描述子判别性。本文重新审视了基于RL的关键点学习，并提出一种充分利用几何一致性信号的奖励，仅从单个正样本对中同时推导出奖励和惩罚，无需与负样本进行对比。这种更丰富的信号提供了足够的监督对比，使得仅从正图像对中学习判别性检测器和描述子成为可能，从而在极其有限的监督下实现表示学习。此外，我们展示了相同的RL目标可扩展到匹配阶段，通过适配LightGlue，将MegaDepth1500上的AUC@5从56.58提升至59.65，并实现了从具有部分视觉重叠的图像对中对完整稀疏匹配流水线进行弱监督训练。我们在公认的基准上验证了所提方法，展示了与全监督方法相比具有竞争力的结果。我们进一步表明，该方法甚至可以在低纹理的医学视频序列上进行训练，而在此类场景中，相机位姿通常不可用，标准的SfM管道也经常失败。代码和数据见 https://github.com/fraunhoferhhi/RIPEpp 。

title: AsymFeX: A Symmetry-Driven Framework for Ischemic Stroke Segmentation Across Imaging Modalities and Stroke Stages
summary: Fast and accurate segmentation of Acute Ischemic Stroke (AIS) lesions is essential for stroke prognosis and treatment planning. Non-contrast CT (NCCT), the first-line imaging modality for diagnosing ischemic infarcts, exhibits subtle infarct contrast, making manual delineation slow and labor-intensive. Motivated by this, and by the clinical practice of comparing brain hemispheres to localize infarcts, we propose a two-stage, nnU-Net-compatible 3D segmentation method. The first stage corrects head tilt to align each scan to its true anatomical mid-sagittal plane; the second applies a novel Asymmetric Feature Extraction (AsymFeX) module, comparing each voxel to its true contralateral counterpart within a local 3 x 3 x 3 neighborhood via cross-hemispheric attention, feature disparity estimation, and dual-scale gating to capture both large and small infarcts. On AISD, our method achieves 0.6796 Dice, 23.53 mm HD95, and 7.69 mL AVD, significantly outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods, with clinically relevant volumetric analysis at the 70 mL thrombolysis-eligibility threshold. Proof-of-concept evaluation on ATLAS v2.1 and ISLES'24 demonstrates that the same symmetry-driven design generalizes across imaging modalities and stroke time points without architectural changes, further supported by an uncertainty analysis assessing reliability under clinical deployment. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/biomedia-lab/AIS-detection.
tldr: Proposes a two-stage 3D segmentation framework for acute ischemic stroke that first corrects head tilt to align to the mid-sagittal plane, then applies an asymmetric feature extraction module using cross-hemispheric attention and disparity estimation to capture infarcts, achieving state-of-the-art results across multiple modalities and stroke stages.
tldr_zh: 提出一个两阶段3D分割框架用于急性缺血性卒中，首先矫正头部倾斜以对齐至正中矢状面，然后应用不对称特征提取模块，通过跨半球注意力和差异估计捕捉梗死灶，在多种模态和卒中阶段取得最先进结果。
summary_zh: 急性缺血性卒中（AIS）病灶的快速精确分割对于卒中预后评估和治疗规划至关重要。非增强CT（NCCT）作为诊断缺血性梗死的一线影像学手段，其病灶对比度微弱，导致手动勾画耗时且费力。基于此，并结合临床中通过比较大脑半球来定位梗死的实践，我们提出了一种两阶段、兼容nnU-Net的3D分割方法。第一阶段校正头部倾斜，使每个扫描图像对齐至真实的解剖学正中矢状面；第二阶段应用新型不对称特征提取（AsymFeX）模块，通过跨半球注意力、特征差异估计以及双尺度门控机制，将每个体素与其在局部3×3×3邻域内的真实对侧对应体元进行比较，从而捕获大小不一的梗死病灶。在AISD数据集上，我们的方法达到了0.6796 Dice、23.53 mm HD95和7.69 mL AVD，显著优于现有最先进方法，并在70 mL溶栓资格阈值上实现了具有临床意义的体积分析。在ATLAS v2.1和ISLES'24数据集上的概念验证评估表明，这种对称驱动的设计无需改变架构即可泛化至不同成像模态和卒中时间点，通过评估临床部署可靠性的不确定性分析进一步支持了该结论。代码公开于https://github.com/biomedia-lab/AIS-detection。

title: Explainable Transformer Models for Clinical Prediction Tasks on Structured Electronic Health Records
summary: Predictive models over structured electronic health records (EHRs) remain central to machine learning for healthcare, but few have jointly emphasized quantitative laboratory information and interpretability with respect to input medical events. We present BERT-LER, a BERT-style model for coded EHR timelines pretrained and fine-tuned from a de-identified EHR dataset of 75 million patients, that encodes laboratory test results as discrete tokens while retaining graded information through percentile-based binning, paired with Integrated Gradients for token-level attributions grounded in the input EHR sequence. We benchmark our approach on the public EHRShot benchmark suite and on an asthma severity progression study based on real-world data. This addresses a methodological gap in EHR foundation-style modeling by unifying laboratory value representation and explainability in a single framework, while assessing whether both predictive performance and explanations generalize beyond standard clinical prediction tasks. Across EHRShot and asthma tasks, BERT-LER achieves predictive performance that is competitive with, and on laboratory-related tasks often exceeds, publicly available benchmark models, and provides attributions that align with clinically known risk factors. Our architecture and explainability approach can be applied to many therapeutic areas and prediction tasks using language models trained on structured EHRs.
tldr: The paper proposes BERT-LER, a BERT-style model for structured EHRs that encodes lab test results as discrete tokens with percentile-based binning and uses Integrated Gradients for explainability, achieving competitive predictive performance on clinical benchmarks.
tldr_zh: 该论文提出了BERT-LER，一种用于结构化电子健康记录的BERT风格模型，将实验室检测结果通过百分位分箱编码为离散令牌，并使用集成梯度进行可解释性，在临床基准测试中取得了具有竞争力的预测性能。
summary_zh:
摘要：  
基于结构化电子健康记录（EHR）的预测模型仍是医疗机器学习领域的核心，但很少有模型同时兼顾定量实验室检验信息的利用以及对输入医疗事件的可解释性。我们提出了BERT-LER，一种基于BERT风格的模型，用于编码EHR时间序列，该模型在包含7500万患者的去标识化EHR数据集上进行了预训练和微调。模型将实验室检验结果编码为离散词元，同时通过基于百分位数的分箱保留分级信息，并结合Integrated Gradients方法，实现基于输入EHR序列的词元级归因。我们在公开的EHRShot基准测试套件以及一项基于真实世界数据的哮喘严重程度进展研究上对方法进行了评估。本研究通过将实验室数值表示与可解释性统一于单一框架，弥补了EHR基础模型建模的方法论空白，同时评估了预测性能与解释性是否能够泛化至标准临床预测任务之外。在EHRShot和哮喘任务中，BERT-LER的预测性能与公开可用的基准模型相当，在涉及实验室检验的任务中通常更优，并且其归因结果与临床已知的风险因素一致。我们的架构与可解释性方法可应用于多个治疗领域及预测任务，只需使用在结构化EHR上训练的语言模型即可。

title: Towards Clinically Faithful Medical Image Captioning via Enhanced Vision-Language Alignment
summary: Medical image captioning is a technique that accelerates early-stage diagnostic workflows and enhances the interpretability of medical diagnostic AI systems. However, unlike general image captioning, clinically reliable captioning remains challenging due to grayscale-based modalities, subtle anatomical cues, specialized medical phrasing, and variations in data quality. Despite recent advances in large vision-language models, fluent outputs do not necessarily guarantee sufficient alignment with clinical concept spaces or evaluation criteria. To address this issue, we propose a framework that strengthens clinical alignment by separating and enhancing training-time alignment and inference-time alignment. We build a medical image captioning pipeline that integrates single/dual vision encoders based on BioMedCLIP and SigLIP2, a Q-Former, and a LLaMA-based decoder, and examine the contribution of auxiliary learning for UMLS concept/type prediction. At inference, we apply single-embedding-based reranking to select the best caption among candidates, while at training we introduce MedPAIR-SCST, which combines clinically relevant rewards to shift the generative distribution toward improved clinical alignment. Our experiments show that complementary visual representations with a multi-encoder design and concept-level auxiliary learning help preserve clinically meaningful information. Furthermore, inference-time reranking provides a practical way to improve semantic and clinical alignment without additional training, whereas MedPAIR-SCST goes beyond selection by directly improving the model's distribution to generate more consistent and clinically grounded captions. These findings suggest that jointly leveraging selection-based alignment and reinforcement-learning-based alignment can promote more trustworthy medical image captioning even in data-constrained settings.
tldr: This paper proposes a framework for clinically faithful medical image captioning that enhances vision-language alignment through separated training-time (MedPAIR-SCST with clinically relevant rewards) and inference-time (reranking) alignment, using a multi-encoder design with BioMedCLIP/SigLIP2, Q-Former, and LLaMA decoder, and demonstrates improved clinical grounding even in data-constrained settings.
tldr_zh: 本文提出一个用于临床可信的医学图像描述框架，通过分离训练时（使用临床相关奖励的MedPAIR-SCST）和推理时（重新排序）对齐来增强视觉-语言对齐，采用BioMedCLIP/SigLIP2的多编码器设计、Q-Former和LLaMA解码器，证明即使在数据受限环境下也能改善临床接地性。
summary_zh: 医学影像描述是一种加速早期诊断流程并增强医学诊断AI系统可解释性的技术。然而，与通用影像描述不同，由于基于灰度影像的模态、细微的解剖学提示、专业的医学表述以及数据质量的差异，临床可靠的描述仍然具有挑战性。尽管大型视觉-语言模型近期取得了进展，流畅的输出并不一定能保证与临床概念空间或评估标准充分对齐。为解决这一问题，我们提出了一个通过分离并增强训练时对齐与推理时对齐来强化临床对齐的框架。我们构建了一个医学影像描述流水线，集成了基于BioMedCLIP和SigLIP2的单/双视觉编码器、Q-Former以及基于LLaMA的解码器，并探讨了辅助学习对UMLS概念/类型预测的贡献。在推理阶段，我们采用基于单嵌入的重排序从候选描述中选出最佳结果；在训练阶段，我们引入了MedPAIR-SCST，该方法结合临床相关奖励，将生成分布向改善的临床对齐方向偏移。实验表明，采用多编码器设计的互补视觉表示以及概念级辅助学习有助于保留临床有意义的信息。此外，推理时重排序提供了一种无需额外训练即可改善语义与临床对齐的实用方法，而MedPAIR-SCST则超越简单选择，通过直接优化模型分布以生成更一致且基于临床的描述。这些发现表明，联合利用基于选择的对齐与基于强化学习的对齐，即使在数据受限的条件下也能促进更可靠的医学影像描述。

title: MOSAIC: Modality-agnostic Spectral Alignment for Federated Image-level Weakly Supervised Tumor Segmentation under Client-specific Missing Modalities
summary: Trustworthy multimodal fusion in clinical settings requires handling incomplete and heterogeneous modality subsets across institutions, where privacy constraints prohibit centralized data sharing. Federated learning (FL) mitigates data-sharing constraints but suffers from client-specific missing modalities, where institutions possess incomplete multimodal subsets, degrading fusion quality and segmentation performance. While FL and weak supervision have been studied separately, their joint use with image-level labels under heterogeneous missing modalities remains unaddressed. We propose \textbf{MOSAIC}, the first modality-agnostic federated framework for weakly supervised binary tumor segmentation under client-specific missing modalities. We introduce a client-specific modality-alignment module that fuses available channels into a shared latent space without prior knowledge of modality identity, a spectral prototype alignment loss that reconciles cross-client distribution shift using compact non-invertible frequency-domain statistics, and a dedicated federated refinement network that denoises the resulting CAM pseudo-labels into accurate masks, breaking the accuracy ceiling of weak supervision. Experiments on three multi-institutional brain tumor benchmarks (FeTS2022, BraTS-MEN, and BraTS-SSA) demonstrate significant improvements over all image, box, and point-supervised baselines, approaching fully supervised accuracy using only image-level labels and reaching 0.84 Dice on FeTS2022. Dynamic new client addition enables previously unseen institutions to join an already-trained federation within 0.01-0.04 Dice without retraining. Code is available at https://github.com/Tarun2201/MOSAIC.
tldr: MOSAIC is a federated learning framework for weakly supervised tumor segmentation that handles client-specific missing modalities by aligning heterogeneous multimodal inputs into a shared latent space using spectral prototype alignment and a refinement network, achieving near fully-supervised accuracy with only image-level labels.
tldr_zh: MOSAIC是一种联邦学习框架，用于弱监督肿瘤分割，通过光谱原型对齐和细化网络将客户端特定的缺失模态异构多模态输入对齐到共享潜在空间，仅使用图像级标签即可达到接近全监督的精度。
summary_zh:
摘要：
在临床环境中实现可信的多模态融合需要处理跨机构的不完整和异构模态子集，而隐私约束禁止中心化数据共享。联邦学习（FL）缓解了数据共享限制，但面临客户端特定的模态缺失问题——机构拥有不完整的多模态子集，导致融合质量和分割性能下降。尽管FL和弱监督已分别得到研究，但在异构缺失模态下结合图像级标签的联合使用仍未得到解决。我们提出\textbf{MOSAIC}，这是首个针对客户端特定缺失模态下弱监督二元肿瘤分割的模态无关联邦框架。我们引入了客户端特定模态对齐模块，无需模态身份先验知识即可将可用通道融合到共享潜在空间中；频谱原型对齐损失，利用紧凑不可逆的频域统计量协调跨客户端分布偏移；以及专用联邦细化网络，将生成的CAM伪标签去噪为精确掩膜，突破了弱监督的精度上限。在三个多机构脑肿瘤基准（FeTS2022、BraTS-MEN和BraTS-SSA）上的实验表明，该方法在所有图像、框和点监督基线中均取得了显著改进，仅使用图像级标签即可接近全监督精度，并在FeTS2022上达到0.84 Dice。动态新客户端加入使得未见过的机构无需重新训练即可在0.01-0.04 Dice范围内加入已训练的联邦。代码可在https://github.com/Tarun2201/MOSAIC获取。
